title: RRB NTPC: choose the right CEN, post and CBT preparation path
description: Separate NTPC graduate and undergraduate applications, post-specific typing or aptitude tasks, and new recruitment from older answer-key notices.
intro: Graduate and undergraduate NTPC recruitment share a familiar name, but their notifications, eligibility and post choices are separate. The unified RRB portal lists detailed CEN 06/2026 and 07/2026 notices. This guide helps you use the correct one without confusing it with the older 2025 CBT 2 key.

sections.title: Create a cycle-and-level label
sections.body:
Write the CEN number, graduate/undergraduate level and selected RRB at the top of your notes. Match all three before opening an application, key or result link. A notice for CEN 07/2025 is not an announcement for CEN 07/2026.

Read the detailed notification rather than treating an earlier indicative advertisement as the full rulebook. Check qualification cut-off, post parameters, language, medical standard and permitted application choices. The [NTPC hub](/exams/rrb-ntpc/) links the two current detailed notices. If a later corrigendum changes a rule or vacancy, retain it with the original CEN.

sections.title: Compare posts by work and additional tests
sections.body:
Do not choose only by a pay figure or popularity poll. Record the post's job setting, shift expectations, medical requirements and any typing or aptitude task. A clerical post and an operating post can need different preparation after CBT 2.

Use the post parameters in your CEN to decide whether your qualification and medical eligibility fit. Then make a preference order you can explain. An aptitude requirement does not apply to every NTPC post; nor does typing. Keep a separate practice block for the additional task required by the posts you actually select.

sections.title: Prepare the three common CBT subjects together
sections.body:
In maths, build fraction, percentage, ratio and rate fluency before longer calculations. In reasoning, explain the relationship or constraint instead of memorising the answer pattern. For general awareness, combine static concepts with dated current-affairs revision.

Use mixed sets regularly so you must choose the method yourself. After a mock, classify unfinished questions as unknown, too slow or poorly selected. Retry the “too slow” group with a simpler representation. Follow [data interpretation](/quant/data-interpretation/) and [coding-decoding](/reasoning/coding-decoding/) when those are the bottlenecks. Check the official stage rules before deciding the mock duration.

sections.title: Handle older keys as a separate archive
sections.body:
The CEN 07/2025 undergraduate CBT 2 objection window ran in September and is labelled ended on our [answer-key archive](/exam-updates/rrb-ntpc-ug-2025-cbt-2-answer-key/). Saving an old paper can help revision, but an old login is not evidence that a new recruitment's answer key exists.

When your own stage's key appears, save responses and question IDs, calculate raw marks using that paper's rule, and challenge only with evidence inside the stated window. Keep normalised marks and qualification separate from a personal estimate. Follow the matching board's official result list for the actual next-stage decision.

drills.prompt: A train travels 180 km in 3 hours. At the same speed, how far in 2.5 hours?
drills.explanation: Speed is 180 ÷ 3 = 60 km/h. Distance is 60 × 2.5 = 150 km. Keep hours and kilometres consistent.

drills.prompt: A CEN 07/2025 response-sheet link appears while you are applying under 07/2026. Is it your current key?
drills.explanation: Recruitment number and year must match. Similar names and the same post level do not make the documents interchangeable.

checklist: Write my exact CEN and recruitment level.
Map additional typing or aptitude tasks to my posts.
Keep old key archives separate from my application cycle.

faqs.q: Does every NTPC post require typing?
faqs.a: No. Follow the post-specific selection stages in the detailed CEN.

faqs.q: Can I treat an indicative notice as the final eligibility rule?
faqs.a: Use the detailed CEN and subsequent official corrigenda for the full conditions.
